test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 23 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: D, E, F, G, L, M and N are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Only one person sits between L and E when counted from the left of E. G sits third to the right of N. M sits third to the left of F. G sits to the immediate right of M. D is not an immediate neighbour of M. How many people sit between D and E when counted from the right of D?
solution:
Given: D, E, F, G, L, M and N are sitting around a circular table facing the centre.

1) G sits third to the right of N.

2) G sits to the immediate right of M. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1e882b43114315754bbf878e63411c8e46095d5faeff13139479cac7c0eb7b30.png] 

3) M sits third to the left of F.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/576d543a6b08b4325a2931825153ebf3b2a66ebcd17c91286597544600bee55f.png] 

4) D is not an immediate neighbour of M. 

5) Only one person sits between L and E when counted from the left of E.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b9305aa1ec51779dd8d1052e931a72887c754f3df683f0e4fe83e941c59eb23.png] 

Thus, according to the final arrangement, three people sit between D and E when counted from the right of D.

Hence, "Option 1" is the correct answer.
